title: A note on the A.C. spectrum of limit-periodic Jacobi matrices
abstract: We show that limit-periodic Jacobi matrices in the weak exponential class $EC(η)$ have purely absolutely continuous spectral type when $η$ is sufficiently large, depending only on the $R$-boundedness constant. The proof first establishes homogeneity of the spectrum from the weak exponential approximation rate. A closure theorem for reflectionless Jacobi matrices then transfers reflectionlessness from the periodic approximants to the limit, and a theorem of Poltoratski and Remling rules out singular spectrum on a homogeneous set.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the spectral properties of limit-periodic Jacobi matrices, which model quantum systems with quasi-periodic potentials. By imposing conditions related to the weak exponential decay of the approximation error, the authors prove that the spectrum must be purely absolutely continuous. This result is significant for understanding the nature of energy spectra in complex, non-periodic quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the spectral type, specifically proving it is purely absolutely continuous, for limit-periodic Jacobi matrices.
main_result: If the matrix belongs to the weak exponential class $EC(\eta)$ with a sufficiently large $\eta$, the Jacobi matrix is proven to have a purely absolutely continuous spectrum.
method: The proof combines establishing spectral homogeneity from the weak exponential approximation rate, transferring reflectionlessness from periodic approximants, and applying theorems to rule out singular spectral components.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the limit-periodic Jacobi matrix, $J$, acting on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$, defined by coefficients $\{a_n\}$ and $\{b_n\}$. These matrices are motivated by connections to quantum dynamics.
key_observables: Spectral type (purely absolutely continuous), spectral bands, and band lengths.
important_parameters: The R-boundedness constant $R$ and the exponential decay rate $\eta$ are critical parameters determining the validity of the result.
main_assumptions: The analysis requires the R-boundedness assumption ($J \in J(R)$) and the condition that the approximation error decays according to the weak exponential class $EC(\eta)$ with $\eta$ large enough.
paper_structure: The structure follows establishing spectral homogeneity from the weak exponential class, followed by using a closure theorem to transfer reflectionlessness, and finally applying a theorem (Poltoratski and Remling) to rule out singular spectrum.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous spectral characterization for quasi-periodic Hamiltonians, which are central models in condensed matter physics for studying localization and spectral gaps in disordered or quasi-periodic potentials.
